"Watch how LPG cylinders are tested under extreme pressure."

Safety is the absolute priority when dealing with highly pressurized gas, which is why every LPG cylinder undergoes a grueling series of stress tests before it ever reaches your kitchen. Manufacturers subject these steel containers to a hydrostatic pressure test, filling them with water at forces far exceeding their normal operating capacity to ensure the structural integrity of the metal. Engineers monitor the vessel for any signs of bulging, cracking, or catastrophic failure to guarantee it can handle the volatile contents safely. If a cylinder shows even the slightest deviation or weakness, it is immediately decommissioned and sent to be recycled. This rigorous quality control process is the invisible shield that prevents accidents and keeps homes around the world secure. It is a fascinating, high-stakes look at the industrial standards that govern the objects we often take for granted.

Water Inside LPG Cylinder? Here’s Why

Ever wondered why LPG cylinders are sometimes filled with water instead of gas? This process is called hydrostatic testing, used to check the cylinder’s strength and pressure tolerance. During this test, water is filled inside and pressure is increased beyond normal limits to detect any leaks or weaknesses. If the cylinder slightly expands, it’s still monitored for safety. But if it fails the test, it is immediately discarded as scrap to prevent any future accidents. This ensures that only safe cylinders reach consumers.

There is significant confusion regarding LPG (cooking gas) rule changes. While several reports and social media posts have claimed new restrictions will take effect on May 1, 2026, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has officially clarified that no changes have been made to refill booking timelines. 

Official Booking & Delivery Rules (Current)

The government has dismissed viral claims of a new 35-day waiting period, reiterating that the existing system remains in place: 

Booking Gap: The mandatory interval between two refill bookings continues to be 25 days in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas.

Connection Types: These timelines apply to all domestic connections, including single-cylinder, double-cylinder, and Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) beneficiaries.

OTP Verification: The Delivery Authentication Code (DAC) system is now mandatory. You must share the OTP received on your registered mobile number with the delivery personnel to receive your cylinder.

Annual Limit: Households are generally eligible for up to 12 subsidised cylinders per financial year. 

New "PNG" Rule (Order issued March 2026)

One major policy change that has been officially introduced involves households in areas with existing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) infrastructure: 

LPG Disconnection: Households must switch to a PNG connection where connectivity is available.

Timeline: LPG supply to such households may be discontinued 3 months after receiving a notice from the gas company.

Exemption: If a PNG connection is technically infeasible, a "No Objection Certificate" (NOC) must be obtained to continue LPG supply.
